text:
maria: hitting weird burst of 429s in staging during token rotation test, looks like a client storm
devon: ugh, classic thundering herd. are the 429s returning Retry-After?
maria: sometimes yes, but our dev clients see 429 without header and immediately retry with the same short backoff
alex: do they have jitter? our SDK had only fixed exponential backoff until we added jitter last quarter
maria: node sample app doesn't; it's using exponential(500ms)*2^n up to 8s and no randomness
jamie: that will synchronize across many instances after token refresh -> synchronized retries -> another 429 wave :grimacing:
sre-bot: incident-note: observed ~1200 concurrent reconnects at 12:43, CPU spike on inference-manager, 35% error rate (429) for 90s
sandeep: we should treat missing Retry-After as server-asked-fast-fail + client jitter to avoid sync. propose: randomized base + capped exp backoff + server-hint use
devon: concrete change: add a client-side jitter window of ±25% and fallback to randomized uniform jitter when Retry-After absent
alex: also add idempotency-key handling for non-streaming requests so retries aren't destructive. streaming is harder ofc
maria: streaming is the issue for us — token rotates mid-stream and clients reconnect, causing partial duplicate outputs downstream
jamie: can we support a resume token from the runtime? like checkpoint offset to avoid replaying the entire prompt
sandeep: runtime already exposes chunk seq ids for some models but not all. need SDK + runtime contract: resume-token + last-processed-offset
devon: in the interim, we should implement safe-replay guard: if reconnection happens within X ms after token rotation, add a small randomized delay (100-500ms) before resuming the stream
alex: here's a suggested pseudo patch for SDK retry (feel free to copy):
```
backoff = min(base * 2**attempt, max)
jitter = rand.uniform(-0.25, 0.25) * backoff
sleep = backoff + jitter
if resp.headers['Retry-After']:
  sleep = max(sleep, parse_retry_after(resp.headers['Retry-After']))
```
jamie: also, when we see sustained 429s with Retry-After > 10s, route to backup model variant automatically (cheaper/fewer tokens)
prod-bot: deploy-plan: canary sdk-node v1.3.4-jitter to 5% users @ 15:00 UTC
maria: I can reproduce locally with a script: spawn 200 clients, force token refresh, observe synchronized reconnects. will attach gist
devon: please add unit + flaky integration test that simulates missing Retry-After and asserts randomized timing distribution (stats test)
sandeep: ops note — add a server metric: "missing_retry_after_ratio" so we can correlate client storms vs header presence
alex: one more subtlety: some clients use shared HTTP connection pools; if all connections retry at once, pool timeouts cause cascading 502s. need randomized conn backoff too
jamie: for SDK parity: ensure python/go/node all get same jitter defaults and same environment var override (REDWOOD_SDK_RETRY_JITTER=0.25)
maria: agree. for onboarding, update sample-app to include a token-rotation test harness so customers can exercise safe-replay behavior
devon: next steps: maria reproduce + gist, devex to draft SDK PR with pseudo-patch, eng-runtime to spec resume-token interface, SRE to add missing_retry_after metric
alex: assigning: maria (repro), devon (sdk patch), sandeep (metrics), jamie (sample-app + doc), eng-runtime (internals spec)
maria: will do. thanks y'all :thumbsup:
